newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Pepsi in deal to re-enter Venezuelan market.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi in deal to re-enter Venezuelan market.

text.p: PepsiCo has signed a deal with a local bottler allowing it to re-enter the soft drink market that it dominated in Venezuela until it lost a key ally to archrival Coca-Cola Co. last summer.

Pepsi had dominated the Venezuelan soft drink market until August, when the country's leading business group, the Cisneros family, suddenly broke a 47-year-old franchise agreement with the company to form a joint venture with Coca-Cola Co.
The switch left Pepsi without a local bottler and Pepsi's products have virtually disappeared from the local market.

Polar, a leading Venezuelan food and beverage company, said Wednesday it agreed to bottle and distribute Pepsi-Cola in Venezuela as of next month. The venture will be 70 percent controlled by Polar and 30 percent by Pepsi, Polar said.
Distribution will be limited at first to central Venezuela, through Polar affiliate Sopresa, which operates two bottling plants in the states of Aragua and Miranda.
It will subsequently reach the rest of the country over two years through planned investments of $380 million, it said.
Pepsi's stock rose 25 cents to $31.875 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
